subject: gk
question: The concept of ‘Concurrent List’ in the Constitution of India is borrowed from ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Australia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of Australia.
 
• The Concurrent List allows both the Centre and State governments to make laws on the subjects listed within it.
 
• In case of a conflict between the central and state law on a concurrent subject, the central law prevails.
 
• The idea of a Concurrent List aims to ensure uniformity in administrative and legislative matters across the country.
 
• The subjects in the Concurrent List include education, marriage, bankruptcy and insolvency, and social security among others.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union List**

 
 
• The Union List comprises subjects on which only the Central Government can legislate.
 
• Examples include defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and railways.
 
 
 
• **State List**
 
 
• The State List includes subjects on which only the State Governments can legislate.
 
• Examples include police, public health, and agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Residual Powers**
 
 
• Any subject not mentioned in the Union, State, or Concurrent List falls under the residual powers, which are vested in the Central Government.
 
• These subjects are not explicitly listed in the Constitution but are deemed necessary for the country's governance.
